newsitem.title: UK: Dlr/mark eases after Koebnick, awaits U.S. trade.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/mark eases after Koebnick, awaits U.S. trade.

text.p: The dollar eased slightly at the European midsession with dollar/mark a touch softer after comments from Bundesbank member Koebnick and sentiment generally cautious ahead of U.S. trade data later today.
Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Koebnick said earlier he had little objection to dollar/mark around 1.70 but there was no need to expect further weakness of the mark against the dollar.
The dollar eased back from levels just below 1.69 marks before the comments, trading at 1.6851/56 at 1032 GMT and well below late Tuesday's European level of 1.6960/70 marks.
"What he said was a bit mixed so the market is a bit confused and taking it marginally negatively," said Lee Ferridge, currency strategist at Commerzbank in London.

The Federal Reserve's decision to keep rates steady after Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting knocked the dollar lower overnight but expectations of U.S. tightening in the future are still running high, providing a base for the U.S. currency, said analysts.
Focus now is on today's U.S. trade data for March due at 1230 GMT. An average of forecasts points to an overall deficit of $10.3 billion from February's $10.4 billion shortfall.

Dealers said attention will dwell on the U.S./Japan bilateral trade gap for signs of further widening, especially after the concerns of a sustained widening expressed by U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin Tuesday.
"The U.S./Japan component of the U.S. trade figures is not as great as it was but the market is still very wary of the U.S. reaction to a wider gap with Japan," said a U.S. bank dealer.

Dollar/yen was firmer after being pushed lower overnight on reports a Bank of Japan official said the bank was mulling the timing of a rate hike. The BOJ said early today the official was misquoted and there were no immediate plans for a rate increase.
Dollar/yen stood at 113.76/86 at 1115 GMT, down from earlier levels above 114 yen but well above overnight lows below 113 yen.

"Dollar/yen is trying to form a bottom at the moment. The Nikkei was down 500 points overnight and if that continues, the comments out of Japan will probably be more dollar supportive," said Commerzbank's Ferridge.
Elsewhere, the Swiss franc gave up some of its recent gains after the Swiss National Bank said it would significantly add liquidity to stem franc strength.

Dollar/Swiss franc was trading at 1.4030/35 after touching an overnight low of 1.3760 francs. Mark/Swiss franc climbed above 6-1/2 month lows after the SNB announcement and stood at 83.15/17 centimes from an overnight bottom of 82.39.
